name: Alchemist
description: The magister-alchemists of the Gold Wind have a scientific, intellectual reputation, focusing on practical research with applications in the physical world. Members of the Gold Order, they are widely acknowledged as masters of the manipulation of matter.

name: Archer
description: Respected for their skill and command of the battlefield, archers pride themselves on being apart from (and even better than) the usual rabble that joins the army. Anyone can hold a halberd or fire a handgun, they say, but it takes years of training to be an archer.

career_level.name: Archer Captain
trappings: Light Warhorse with Saddle and Tack

name: Artillerist
description: The pride and joy of the Empire, its artillery is famed for an awe-inspiring spectacle that strikes fear into the heart of all her enemies. Artillery regiments do not possess the glamour of the knightly orders or the Greatswords — it is hard graft involving heavy lifting, fetching, carrying, and tedious excavation. Despite this, it is vital to the Empire's war effort and artillerists see themselves as the unsung heroes of the Empire's armies.

career_level.name: Master Artillerist
trappings: Light Warhorse with Saddle and Tack

name: Astromancer
description: Magisters who channel Azyr are astromancers, also known as Celestial Wizards, or 'Blue Wizards' by the uneducated. They favour skullcaps, high-collared cloaks, and expensive robes in deep blues and blacks, emblazoned with silver and gold motifs to represent the night sky. They scrutinise the heavens and draw down the Wind of Azyr to bend the elements to their will and manipulate fate itself.

name: Beadle
description: Professors at the University of Altdorf and wizards at the Colleges of Magic tend to lose themselves in the study of their discipline. That is why these organisations require a staff of a more practical bent; beadles, who guard the college halls, libraries, and laboratories from burglars, spies, and — most of all — misbehaving students.

career_level.name: Laboratory Assistant
trappings: Uniform in the Colours of the Faculty

name: Camp Follower
description: Like mobile cities, the armies of the Old World rely on complex supply chains and strict organisation to keep them fed and supplied. Private enterprise is always on the lookout for profit, so much of any army will be made up of an eclectic band of hangers on, pedlars, bawds, tradespeople, artisans, and charlatans. Those dedicated to following the troops without any specific trade or vocation come under the auspices of Camp Follower.

career_level.name: Camp Chief
trappings: Riding Horse with Saddle and Tack

name: Cartographer
description: As the world gets more sophisticated there is a need to map it in increasing detail. Whether this involves exploring largely unknown lands and making sweeping maps of the general area or going into exacting detail over small tracts in petty land disputes, cartographers are increasingly in demand.

name: Chasseur de Blaireaux
description: Les Chevaucheurs de blaireau sont des figures solitaires qui arpentent le Moot tels des Chevaliers en quête, en plus petits et plus courtauds. L'efficacité constatée des Chevaucheurs de blaireau au combat est littéralement incroyable — les blaireaux, comme les halflings, deviennent étonnamment féroces en cas de menace, capables d'affronter des adversaires bien plus imposants qu'eux-mêmes.

career_level.name: Taquineur de Blaireau
trappings: Tamed Badger with Saddle and Harness

career_level.name: Sergent Blaireau
trappings: Badger Barding (2 AP on Head and Torso)

name: Druid
description: Jade Wizards are more welcome in villages across the Empire than any of the other Imperial Wizards. It is well known they can control plants, and that the land thrives in their presence. Any settlement that welcomes a druid should expect a bumper harvest in the coming year. They tap the vitality of the earth and the power of nature to manipulate the natural world through their magic.

name: Gardechamps
description: Ces halflings courageux patrouillent le long des frontières du Moot, et se servent de leur connaissance poussée du terrain et de leurs tactiques rusées de guérilla pour mettre en déroute les visiteurs clandestins. Les Gardechamps sont avant tout des halflings du peuple, des visages amicaux qui rassurent les citoyens. Les Gardechamps vétérans surprennent souvent les autres aventuriers par leur expérience face à la nécromancie.

name: Greatsword
description: Greatswords are the signature elite infantry of the Imperial armies, the most prestigious and feared of all the Empire's foot soldiers. They forsake the shield to wield huge zweihänder swords, ensuring their combats are short and deadly whichever way they go. Their large, two-handed weapons are unwieldy, so Greatswords need to be swift and athletic to compensate.

career_level.name: Greatsword Sergeant
trappings: Manual on the Art of Zweihänder Fighting

career_level.name: Greatsword Captain
trappings: Light Warhorse with Saddle and Tack

name: Halberdier
description: The mainstay of all Imperial armies, Halberdiers are found in forces the length and breadth of the Empire, and beyond. They have a reputation for reliability and grit and make a formidable sight on the field of battle, massed closely together with their imposing weapons. The Halberdier takes heart from fighting in large groups of tightly formed units, where they benefit from the reach of the halberd while not suffering too much from a lack of manoeuvrability.

career_level.name: Halberdier Captain
trappings: Light Warhorse with Saddle and Tack

name: Handgunner
description: The Handgunner is a comparative newcomer to the Imperial army. Though they have been around for hundreds of years, they are not yet entirely trusted by the rest of the military. Even so, as technology advances, they have become increasingly effective on the battlefield and are fielded in the Imperial armies in ever greater numbers.

career_level.name: Handgunner Captain
trappings: Light Warhorse with Saddle and Tack

name: Hierophant
description: Light Wizards are also known as white wizards, hierophants or, sometimes, exorcists. These wizards usually dress in pristine white clothes, a colour that tends to attract the Light Wind. They are members of the Order of Light, respected for its difficult practise and regarded as exotic and austere.

name: Knight of the Blazing Sun
description: The Knights of the Blazing Sun are templars of Myrmidia and the goddess' largest Order in the Empire. The Blazing Suns are renowned for their study of strategy and tactics in both warfare and personal combat. Myrmidia prizes the enquiring mind, invention, and the cultivation of diverse knowledge, so knights hone their judgement, resourcefulness and skills in diplomacy.

career_level.name: Novice
trappings: Riding Horse with Saddle and Tack

career_level.name: Hochmeister
trappings: Small Unit of Blazing Sun Knights

career_level.name: Knight of the Inner Circle
trappings: Large Unit of Knights or Several Small Units of Knights

name: Knight of the White Wolf
description: There are few sights more evocative of the Ulrican faith than that of a heavily armoured and heroically hirsute knight galloping into battle swinging a cavalry hammer. The Knights of the White Wolf are the largest templar order in the Empire, charged with protecting Ulric's holy sites wherever they are found. Ulric's faithful do not favour passive guard duty, so White Wolves are ever active in the field, hunting down all who threaten the god's worshippers.

career_level.name: Novice
trappings: Riding Horse with Saddle and Tack

career_level.name: Templar Sergeant
trappings: Small Unit of White Wolf Knights

name: Knight Panther
description: The Knights Panther are the most widespread secular order in the Empire, second only to the Reiksguard in power. They are not aligned with any province and will lend military aid to any general or leaders deserving of their support. The Order is celebrated for prowess in battle, a fanatical hatred of mutants and a degree of political acumen which allows them to stay aloof from most petty disputes.

career_level.name: Squire
trappings: Riding Horse with Saddle and Tack

career_level.name: Knight
trappings: Plate Armour and Great Helm with Bestial Crest
Ring or Medallion with Panther Emblem

career_level.name: Company Commander (Inner Circle)
trappings: Large Unit of Knights Panther or Several Small Units of Knights

name: Light Cavalry
description: Tilean mercenary armies rely on fast, lightly armed horsemen to provide mobile striking power. Rather than charge headlong into the teeth of the foe, Tilean light cavalrymen, called Stradioti in their language, prefer to strike from the flanks or, best of all, the rear, where the enemy's baggage train presents a tempting target.

career_level.name: Reiver
trappings: Riding Horse with Saddle and Tack

career_level.name: Captain
trappings: Brace of Pistols with Gunpowder and Ammunition

name: Magister Vigilant
description: Even though the patriarchs of the Colleges refuse to confirm their existence, the lowliest of apprentice wizards have heard of Magisters Vigilant, mages who seek out and destroy those who have broken their oaths and betrayed their order. Each college sponsors a small cadre of Magisters Vigilant, though the Grey College is said to sponsor several of their members to take on the role during their careers.

name: Maneater
description: Maneaters are the Ogres most encountered by denizens of the Empire. These wandering warriors leave their tribes behind to travel across the Old World, in search of novel foes to fight and food to eat. They are popular among commanders who can afford to feed them, as Ogres make excellent shock troops. Maneaters often spend years away from their home in the Mountains of Mourne, enjoying the novel tastes and challenges such an existence brings.

name: Mundane Alchemist
description: Alchemists, being schooled in the properties of matter, are experts at producing new materials and improving existing ones. They can prepare chemical concoctions and often work together with metalworkers. Theirs is a specialised kind of knowledge, and one that is in high demand — the Artillery School in Nuln, for example, keeps a whole department of alchemists tasked with the creation of blackpowder and improving its efficiency.

name: Ogre Butcher
description: Among the Ogres of the Mountains of Mourne, the position of Butcher lies somewhere between that of Priest and Mystic. Their faith is practiced in the preparation of meat; the hanging of a carcass, the slicing of flesh and the spilling of blood are to them as prayer and incense are to the most devout Shallyan. Ogre Butchers are chosen from an early age for indoctrination into the mysteries of the Great Maw, and often earn the Big Name of Mawseeker later in life.

name: Patrouilleur des Karak
description: La sûreté des routes doit être préservée, et un nouveau chemin doit être tracé lorsque l'ancien devient trop dangereux : tel est le devoir des Patrouilleurs des karak. Ces nains endurcis ne doivent leur survie qu'à leur capacité à se préparer. Ils doivent savoir enchaîner chasse, reconnaissance et combat, voire même réparation d'un pont en plein milieu de leur expédition.

name: Pikeman
description: All towns and villages in the Old World have their militias, masses of armed residents who can be turned out on short notice to defend homes and fields or fight for a few weeks in their lord's service. Their lack of discipline and desire to return home to families and trades, however, makes them of limited use on long campaigns or when facing heavily armed and armoured horsemen. Discipline and drill are the pikeman's greatest weapons — a phalanx of Pikemen can stop even the heaviest Imperial knights.

name: Priest of Handrich
description: Though not as common as other cults, Handrichan priests are sought after for their financial sense and discretion. Many do preach sermons, teaching Handrich's tenets of self-reliance and the glories of material wealth, but they more often serve in private capacities, overseeing transactions to ensure honesty or offering financial advice. Most tend to temples found in large trading centres, or join caravans and trade expeditions as part of their service to Handrich.

name: Priest of Myrmidia
description: Myrmidian Priests from the Order of the Righteous Spear and Order of Fury help organise cult meetings, spread its teachings, and lead its ceremonies. They value honour, obedience and tactical martial prowess, in emulation of their patron goddess, Myrmidia. They are often sought as advisors by generals and mercenary commanders, particularly in Tilea and Estalia.

name: Priest of Solkan
description: Priests of Solkan are austere, humourless individuals. During rituals, they wear white and gold robes in the style of ancient Tilea. Many don a golden mask in imitation of their god, with a stylised countenance of implacable fury. Certain priests revere the whole pantheon of Law, fighting a losing battle to reassert their influence in the Old World. Nevertheless, it is the Divine Avenger that dominates their thoughts and actions.

name: Priestess of Rhya
description: Priestesses of Rhya live amongst the common folk. They wander between farms, villages, and sacred sites, talking with people, offering blessings, and keeping a close eye on the land and the pastoral care of their flock. People depend on them to stave off famine, bring new life into the world, and give practical advice on love and matters of the family.

name: Pyromancer
description: Bright Wizards are the most belligerent of all the wizards of the Empire. Though other colleges are known for their particular sort of aggression, and all serve the military in one capacity or another, the Bright College brings shock and awe to the battlefield like none other. The Bright Wizards often adopt a warlike and fearsome appearance, their staffs made of iron and topped with a brazier ready to wield all-consuming flame.

career_level.name: Pyromancer
trappings: Second and Third Keys of Secrets

career_level.name: Master Pyromancer
trappings: Fourth and Fifth Keys of Secrets

career_level.name: Pyromancer Lord
trappings: Sixth and Seventh Keys of Secrets

name: Rhinox Herder
description: Rhinox Herders are those rare Ogres who manage to keep an eye on tomorrow even as they fill their gut today. Their duties include both animal husbandry and care, as well as fighting off other Ogres who wander too close to the animal pens or grazing areas looking for a meal. They trade in fine Rhinox Bulls for breeding, and are always on the lookout for new stock to add to their herd.

career_level.name: Rhinox Master
trappings: Herd of Rhinox or Other Large Beasts
Farmstead or Grazing Rights on a Large Estate

name: Rôdeur Fantôme
description: Les Rôdeurs fantômes sont sans doute la plus mortelle de toutes les menaces que recèlent les forêts antiques du Vieux Monde. La détermination et le savoir-faire avec lesquels ces maîtres archers traquent tout ce qui menace la nature terrifieraient n'importe qui. L'harmonie des Rôdeurs fantômes avec la nature est telle que celle-ci semble presque cacher les traces de leur passage aux yeux indiscrets. Pour les Rôdeurs fantômes, la forêt est sacrée par-dessus tout — ils ne tolèrent aucune transgression.

career_level.name: Esprit du Vent
trappings: Quality Elven Bow and Quality Leather Armour (at least 1 Advantage each)

name: Scryer
description: A scarce few Humans possess an ability to look back into the past, to see what happened in a specific location, with a certain object, or to a certain person they touch. Even fewer people can use that ability without being driven out of their wits. Those people who use this rare ability regularly are known as scryers. They possess the rare ability to infer facts about the past through contact with a person, item, or place.

name: Shaman
description: Amber Wizards are known for their feral appearance and lifestyle, more at home in the wilderness than the town, and with more affinity for animals than their fellow Humans. Many wander the Empire's vast untamed landscape, but just as many find a place they like and settle there. Every village in the Empire has a story of a local monster, giant, or witch who lives in the forest and is to be feared but is seldom encountered — more often than not, this is an Amber Wizard.

career_level.name: Shaman's Apprentice
trappings: Grimoire (often in the form of enscribed bones or teeth)

name: Siege Specialist
description: Though besieging fortified places is common throughout the Old World — an art Humans learned from the Dwarfs — it has reached its highest refinement in Tilea, whose Siege Specialists even Dwarfs will grudgingly admit are 'passable'. It is the Siege Specialist's job to bring down castle walls and to keep others from doing so — letting other poor fools storm the walls while they provide cover, or find a more subtle way in.

name: Spiriter
description: If the wizards of the Gold College are the most accepted by Imperial society, those of the Amethyst College are the least, shunned and avoided whenever possible. There is something about their steady gaze and quiet, grim demeanour that often makes outsiders feel like a corpse laid on a slab. Members of the Amethyst Order, they are feared and respected for their familiarity with death.
